description:
FILED s470bv (Opus, 2026-09-06) while attributing t/uni/method.t's move.
PRE-EXISTING (it was hidden behind an abort until #1221); NOT FIXED HERE.

HOW IT SURFACED.  t/uni/method.t read C 28/21 on the snapshot and reads 31/30
now.  That is a GAIN wearing a loss's numbers, measured: at a3d6d8e it is
28/21, at b25afbc (#1221) it is 31/30.  Before #1221 `utf8::decode($new_utf8)`
was a stub, so `Føø::Bær->$new_utf8` died and ABORTED the whole top-level form
and THIRTEEN perl rows (39-51) were never produced.  They are produced now:
two `->can` rows and two others PASS, the rest fail honestly.  No row went from
a genuine `ok` to `not ok`.

THE RESIDUAL BUG.  Among the newly produced rows, a method call on a package
whose name is not ASCII returns something that stringifies as a BARE
`HASH(0xb)` -- no class prefix, and an address that is not the object's.  perl
prints `Føø::Bær=HASH(0x55...)`.  Two of the file's rows name it:

    Can access nèw as a method when the UTF-8 package name is in a scalar.
    Can access $new_ascii, [new], stored in a scalar, as a method, when the
      UTF-8 package name is in a scalar.

This is the #418 family: a non-ASCII PACKAGE name does not survive the CL
reader (SBCL NFKC-normalises and `:invert` down-cases), so the blessed class
that comes back is not the class that went in, and the stringifier has no name
to print.  s423/s425 pipe-quoted the emission side; what is left is the RUNTIME
side of the same identity -- what `bless` stores and what `p-ref`/the `""`
coercion read back.

REPRODUCER (write it as a probe before fixing):

    package Føø::Bær; sub new { bless {}, shift } sub nèw { 42 }
    package main;
    my $o = Føø::Bær->new;
    print "$o\n";           # perl: Føø::Bær=HASH(0x...)   PCL: HASH(0xb)
    print ref($o), "\n";    # compare too

ACCEPTANCE: the probe's two lines match perl's shape (class prefix present,
`ref` answers the original spelling); guard rows beside the existing #418 ones;
and t/uni/method.t re-measured -- its two rows above are the cheap check.
subject: A method call on a NON-ASCII package returns an object that stringifies `HASH(0xb)` instead of `Føø::Bær=HASH(0x...)` -- the #418 family, seen in t/uni/method.t once #1221 let the file get that far
